## Graphic Standards Manual

Week 1. Establish the graphic system used to communicate all later work.

- [Class 01]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/classes/class-01/) — Week 1 — Aug 25: Begin the Graphic Standards Manual, test a sample sheet and organize your files.

<a id="b02"></a>

## Constructive Solid Geometry

Weeks 2–3. Build editable solids with transformations and Boolean operations.

- [Class 02 · Transformations and Booleans]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/classes/class-02/) — Week 2 — Sep 1: Move, rotate and scale procedurally. Compare solid Boolean operators and begin the massing study.
- [Class 03 · 3D printing]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/classes/class-03/) — Week 3 — Sep 8: Refine the CSG process sheet and instructions. Introduce P2b: prepare the CSG object for 3D printing, including units, orientation and slicing.

<a id="b03"></a>

## Descriptive Geometry

Weeks 4–5. Describe geometry through points, lines, edges and faces, then build a parametric solid.

- [Class 04 · Point to solid]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/classes/class-04/) — Week 4 — Sep 15: Point → Line → Edge → Face → Solid → Boolean. Build the parametric pyramid and reconnect to the CSG project.
- [Class 05 · Your module, material and lighting]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/classes/class-05/) — Week 5 — Sep 22: Build your own module from points and faces, test its parameter ranges, then render it with one material and a deliberate lighting setup for the P3a sheet.

<a id="b04"></a>

## Arrays 1 — loops in 1D, 2D and 3D

Week 6. First of two Arrays classes, paired with the loop tutorial. Use loops and nested loops to build a row, grid and layered array; explain counts, spacing and indices.

- [Class 06 · Arrays 1 — loops in 1D, 2D and 3D; CSG sheet]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/classes/class-06/) — Week 6 — Sep 29: Submit 2.1 by 11:59 PM. Teach loops and nested loops through a 1D row, 2D grid and 3D layers, following the loop tutorial. Explain indices, counts and spacing. Check the CSG print before queueing.

<a id="b04-second"></a>

## Arrays 2 — if/Switch and math functions

Week 7. Second of two Arrays classes. Explain if/Switch selection through façade patterns, then use mathematical functions of X and Y to shape a cube volume. Hexagonal and radial arrays remain optional.

- Class 07 · Arrays 2 — if/Switch and math functions — *not yet released* — Week 7 — Oct 6: Teach if/Switch façade patterns and a cube volume driven by functions of X and Y. Use small examples; hexagonal and radial arrays remain optional. No graded submission during studio reviews.

<a id="b04-support"></a>

## Supported practice — Arrays 1 and 2

Week 8. Check 1D/2D/3D repetition, indices, counts and spacing, conditional façade patterns and the mathematical cube volume. Give feedback on the three array sheets. Hand in the CSG print; no new topic.

- Class 08 · Supported practice — Arrays 1 and 2; CSG print — *not yet released* — Week 8 — Oct 13: Hand in 2.2 in class, with digital documentation by 11:59 PM. Check loops, counts and spacing in 1D/2D/3D arrays, then if/Switch patterns and the mathematical cube volume. Give feedback on all three array sheets and resolve problems before the façade class. No new required topic.

<a id="b05"></a>

## Façade attractors — Project 3

Week 9. One façade-attractor class. Combine one curve and one or two point attractors to drive a panel parameter. The next application of attractors is site analysis in Project 4.

- Class 09 · Façade attractors — Project 3; module deadline — *not yet released* — Week 9 — Oct 20: Submit 3.1. Teach the single façade-attractor class for 3.3, combining one curve and one or two points to drive a panel parameter. Begin the elevation and isometric composition.

<a id="b06"></a>

## Attractor-based site analysis — Project 4

Week 10. Apply attractor measurements to the prepared point cloud using supplied groups. Produce two analytical layers and one design observation for the final project; this is distinct from the façade class.

- Class 10 · Project 4 — site analysis; manual and arrays due — *not yet released* — Week 10 — Oct 27: Submit the manual and 3.2. Begin 4.1 using the prepared point cloud and supplied analysis groups. Apply attractor measurements to make two analytical layers and one design observation. Outline the complete Project 4 path from analysis to a laser-cut model; give brief individual façade feedback.

<a id="b06-volume"></a>

## Generative volume exploration — Project 4

Week 11. Use supplied volume groups to explore three settings of one strategy and select a form for contouring.

- Class 11 · Generative volumes — Project 4 — *not yet released* — Week 11 — Nov 3: Introduce 4.2 using supplied volume groups; explore three settings of one generative strategy and select an isometric result. Check the two site-analysis layers and their connection to the volume.

<a id="b07"></a>

## Contouring, laser-cut preparation and assembly

Week 12. Complete all new required content with a prepared example using the supplied contouring group. Cover spacing, numbered parts, cutting-file preparation, material/kerf tests, registration, simple assembly and final documentation. Introduce both 4.3 and 4.4; continue their production during Weeks 13–15.

- Class 12 · Contouring, laser-cut preparation and assembly — final new content — *not yet released* — Week 12 — Nov 10: Check the selected volume and introduce 4.3 and 4.4. Demonstrate the supplied contouring group, spacing, numbered cutting layouts, material/kerf tests, registration, simple assembly and documentation. Use a prepared example to cover the complete fabrication workflow; students refine their own work during Weeks 13–15. This is the last class introducing required content.

<a id="b08"></a>

## Production, feedback and documentation

Weeks 13–15. No new required content. Week 13 checks contours and assembly tests; Week 14 checks fabrication progress and a booklet spread. Week 15 supports production, revisions and final documentation during studio reviews, with no graded submission that day.

- Class 13 · Production and feedback — contours and assembly tests; façade deadline — *not yet released* — Week 13 — Nov 17: Submit 3.3. Review numbered contours, the cutting layout, assembly diagram and a small material or registration test. Refine files and begin production with individual feedback. No new required topic.
- Class 14 · Production and feedback — laser-cut assembly; site deadline — *not yet released* — Week 14 — Nov 24: Submit 4.1. Check tested samples, cutting progress, assembly and the remaining-work plan. Review a booklet spread and provide individual fabrication and presentation feedback. No new required topic.
- Class 15 · Connection tests, production and documentation — *not yet released* — Week 15 — Dec 1: No graded submission during studio reviews. Use ungraded support to check connections, part files, fabrication progress and final documentation.
